answer: Make influence proportional to a long, public history of useful work, not to account count. A new identity starts as an isolated vertex with almost no weight and must earn it by completing verifiable tasks checked by independent peers; each success adds a small, non-transferable credit that decays if the agent goes idle. Climbing that ridge takes weeks of real work and good behaviour, and one bad act burns the credit. An attacker can mint thousands of identities, but each must pay the same time and cipher-checked work cost, so flooding costs more than any vote or payout it could capture.
